tasks.title: Install Leaflet and react-leaflet dependencies
tasks.objective: Add leaflet, react-leaflet, and @types/leaflet to client/package.json and install them so subsequent tasks can import mapping components.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: pnpm install succeeds and lockfile is updated

tasks.no_test_reason: Dependency installation -- validated by successful install and type-check in subsequent tasks
tasks.technical_notes: ADR-001 specifies Leaflet + react-leaflet + OpenStreetMap. No API key needed. Keep versions aligned: react-leaflet 5.x requires leaflet 1.9.x. Run pnpm install from the repository root after editing client/package.json.

tasks.title: Rewrite BeachMap component with Leaflet MapContainer, TileLayer, and markers
tasks.objective: Replace the SVG-based BeachMap implementation with a Leaflet MapContainer rendering OpenStreetMap tiles and custom divIcon markers for all 9 beaches. Preserve the existing BeachMapProps interface. Implement map configuration (center, zoom bounds), custom marker rendering with ocean/shore design tokens, click handling (onSelectBeach callback or navigate), and OpenStreetMap attribution.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: BeachMap renders a Leaflet MapContainer centered at approximately [49.277, -123.155] with default zoom 12
TileLayer uses OpenStreetMap URL pattern https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png with attribution
All 9 beaches from BEACHES array render as Marker components with custom divIcon
Clicking a marker calls onSelectBeach with correct beach ID when callback is provided
Clicking a marker navigates to /beach/{beachId} when onSelectBeach is not provided
Map constrains zoom to min 10, max 16, and sets maxBounds to Vancouver coastal area
acceptance_criteria.test_assertion: Leaflet MapContainer props include minZoom={10}, maxZoom={16}, maxBounds defined

tasks.technical_notes: Import leaflet/dist/leaflet.css at the top of the component. Use L.divIcon for custom markers with inline styles referencing design token hex values (ocean-500: #00bcd4, shore-500: #009688, ocean-600: #00acc1) since Leaflet divIcon renders outside React's className scope. The BeachMapProps interface MUST remain unchanged: { selectedBeachId?: string; onSelectBeach?: (beachId: string) => void }. Leaflet requires DOM mocking in jsdom -- the MapContainer may need a test wrapper or mock. Add a CSS class 'beach-marker' to each divIcon container for testability. Pan/zoom interactions (AC-004 through AC-008) are built-in Leaflet behaviors that do not require custom code -- they are enabled by default on MapContainer. M-3 note: No CSP headers exist in this project, so no CSP changes are needed for tile loading.

tasks.title: Add marker visual states (selected, favorite, hover tooltip) and dark mode support
tasks.objective: Implement the four marker visual states (default, favorite, selected, hover/tooltip) using design token colors, and add dark mode support with CSS filter on the tile layer and inverted tooltip styling. Address spec review notes M-1 (dark mode tooltip) and M-2 (testable dark mode assertion).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When selectedBeachId matches a beach, that marker renders with ocean-600 background, 1.3x scale, 3px white border, and ocean-md shadow
When a beach is a favorite, its marker renders with shore-500 background and a white heart character
Each marker has a Tooltip component showing the beach name, positioned above the marker with direction='top'
When dark class is on the html element, the .leaflet-tile-pane has CSS filter: brightness(0.7) invert(1) contrast(1.1) hue-rotate(200deg) saturate(0.3)
In dark mode, tooltips use sand-50 (#fafafa) background and sand-900 (#212121) text, inverted from light mode (M-1 fix)
Default (non-selected, non-favorite) markers render with ocean-500 background, white 2px border, and ocean-sm shadow

tasks.technical_notes: M-1 resolution: WIREFRAMES.md specifies dark mode tooltips should use sand-50 bg and sand-900 text (inverted from light mode). The TECHNICAL_DESIGN only specified light mode tooltip styling -- implementer must add dark mode tooltip CSS. M-2 resolution: AC-014 originally said 'no jarring bright contrast' which is untestable. The testable replacement is to assert that the CSS filter property on .leaflet-tile-pane contains 'invert(1)' when dark class is present on html element. Dark mode filter CSS should be defined in a <style> tag or CSS module scoped to the BeachMap component. Marker inline styles must use hex values directly since divIcon renders outside Tailwind's className processing. The map container wrapper div should have dark mode classes: dark:bg-sand-800. Responsive aspect ratio: 16/9 on desktop (>=768px), 4/3 on mobile (<768px) per WIREFRAMES.md.
